Bristlecone v1.4.0

This one is about weather, because on a mountain the weather is half the map.

The Conditions tab now opens with a Mountain weather card. It gives you an estimate for where you are and for the highest ground nearby: temperature with a likely range, whether anything falling would be rain or snow, the snow level, the freezing level, and wind with gusts. There's also a little table that steps up the mountain, so you can see where rain turns to snow on the way up. If it's raining and 40° in Millinocket, it'll tell you it's probably snowing on Katahdin.

It's built from the National Weather Service forecast and nearby weather stations (including the high-elevation SNOTEL sites out West), Environment Canada's forecast and stations north of the border, recent trail reports, and the shape of the terrain itself. Ridges and summits get the wind they actually get, not what the airport down the valley is reporting. It's a model estimate, not a measurement, and the card says so. The official forecasts and alerts are right below it, and your own eyes and ears outrank all of it. If you'd rather not see it, you can turn it off in Settings.

Privacy got another pass:

- The "hide where you start and end" setting now hides everything within 650 feet of your start and finish in a straight line, not just the first and last 650 feet of the route. Before, if a trip looped around the block or doubled back past the driveway, a shared route could still show a point right at your house. That's fixed.
- The app's own pages are locked down further, so nothing but Bristlecone's own code can run inside it.

A few other fixes:

- Saving a backup over an older one on Android could leave a broken file. Backups and exports now replace the old file cleanly.
- If Android shut the app down mid-hike at just the wrong moment, part of the recorded trip could go missing when you opened it later. Now only the one damaged point is skipped.
- When Android restarts a recording, it keeps your pause and your step count instead of resetting them.
- Deleting a map download while it was still downloading no longer brings it back from the dead.
- A damaged backup file can't fill up your phone or crash the app when you restore it.
- The About screen now credits Krummholz AI LLC.

Downloads

- Android (8.0 and up): Bristlecone-1.4.0-android.apk. Open it on your phone and allow the install when Android asks. This is still a test build, so a future Play Store version will need a fresh install.
- iPhone and iPad (iOS 16 and up): Bristlecone-1.4.0-ios-unsigned.ipa. For now this installs through AltStore or SideStore.

If something breaks or feels off, let me know. Safe adventures.
